title: Carry the retryable bit on wave bucket rows and the ledger worker row
action: D3 (1ef811f7) for waves. (1) wave_ledger.rs WorkerRow (line 79) gains `pub(crate) retryable: Option<bool>` with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` so old ledgers still parse and the key appears only when set (no-new-key law). (2) wave.rs: where a worker lands in a bucket (~479-486) and where the wave JSON is built (~675-693), set retryable per worker: `true` for send_failed and flipped_before_send (the worker did no work), `false` for timed_out and unverifiable_after_send; a spawn failure, if the wave tracks one, is `true`. Emit the same bit in the per-worker JSON rows of the wave output (never on the bucket count summary). Reuse the outcome→retryable rule hcc-3 added in run.rs if it is a callable fn; otherwise a 6-line match here with a comment naming run.rs's rule as the source. Tests: a send_failed worker row carries retryable true, an unverifiable_after_send row carries false, a done row carries no key, and an old ledger line without the key still parses.

truths: retryable true only for send_failed, flipped_before_send, spawn_failed
done rows carry no retryable key
old ledger rows without the key still parse

artifacts.substantive: per-worker bit in buckets and JSON rows + tests
